거실.x: My family is watching TV in the living room.
거실.e: Literally 'living room' — word for word like English!

괜찮다.m: okay, all right, fine; not bad, decent
괜찮다.x: The color of these clothes looks nice.
괜찮다.e: Shortened from 괜하지 않다. 괜찮아요 = 'It's okay.'
괜찮다.t: 괜찮아요 can also politely decline an offer: 'No thanks, I'm fine.' Pronounced [괜찬타].

데려오다.x: Can I bring a friend to the party today?
데려오다.e: 데리다 (to have someone with you) + 오다 (to come): bring someone here.

기뻐하다.m: to be glad, to be happy (about), to rejoice
기뻐하다.ex: 부모님이 제 합격 소식을 듣고 많이 기뻐하셨어요.
기뻐하다.x: My parents were very happy to hear I'd passed.
기뻐하다.t: Use -어하다 for other people's feelings: 저는 기뻐요, but 친구가 기뻐해요.

불안하다.x: I feel anxious because of tomorrow's test.
불안하다.t: The prefix 불- 'not' becomes 부- before ㄷ or ㅈ: 불안, but 부족 'lack'.

못생기다.m: to be ugly, to be unattractive
못생기다.x: Our puppy is ugly, but so cute.
못생기다.e: 못 'poorly' + 생기다 'to be formed' — the opposite of 잘생기다.

썰다.forms: 썰어요 · 썰었어요 · 썰 거예요 · 써세요 (ㄹ drops)
썰다.m: to slice, to cut (with a knife)
썰다.ex: 먼저 양파와 감자를 얇게 썰어 주세요.
썰다.x: First, please slice the onions and potatoes thinly.
썰다.t: Use 썰다 for food and knives; use 자르다 for paper, hair or scissors.

이모.m: aunt (mother's sister); friendly term for a middle-aged woman
이모.x: My aunt is three years younger than my mom.
이모.t: Restaurant customers often call the server 이모 to sound warm and friendly.

다음 주.x: I have a test next Monday.

오랫동안.forms: 오랫동안 + verb; 오랜만에 = after a long time
오랫동안.ex: 우리는 그 가게 앞에서 오랫동안 기다렸어요.
오랫동안.x: We waited in front of that store for a long time.
오랫동안.t: Pronounced [오래똥안] — the ㅅ in the middle makes 동 tense.

일기.ex: 저는 매일 밤 자기 전에 일기를 써요.
일기.x: I write in my diary every night before bed.
일기.t: Keep a diary with 일기를 쓰다; a different 일기 means 'weather', as in 일기 예보.

안과.x: My eyes were red and sore, so I went to the eye doctor.

위험.x: There are many dangers in the mountains in winter, so be careful.
위험.t: 위험해요! is the everyday way to shout 'Watch out, it's dangerous!'

사례.ex: 이 책에는 다양한 성공 사례가 나와요.
사례.x: This book contains various success stories.
사례.t: A homonym 사례 means 'thanks, reward', as in 사례금 'reward money'.

필수.x: This class is required for all first-year students.
필수.t: Pronounced [필쑤] — the ㅅ tenses after ㄹ.

우려.ex: 물가 상승에 대한 우려가 커지고 있습니다.
우려.x: Concerns about rising prices are growing.
우려.t: 우려 is formal and typical of the news; in daily conversation, use 걱정.

인권.x: Everyone's human rights must be respected.
인권.t: Pronounced [인꿘], with a tense ㄲ sound.

떠오르다.forms: 떠올라요 · 떠올랐어요 · 떠오를 거예요 · 떠오른 (+noun) (르 irregular)
떠오르다.m: to rise, come up; to come to mind
떠오르다.x: A good idea came to me while I was showering.
떠오르다.t: 생각이 떠오르다 (an idea comes to you) vs. 생각을 떠올리다 (you call up a thought).

주도하다.m: to lead, to take the initiative, to spearhead
주도하다.e: Literally 'to guide as the main one'.

안주.m: food eaten with alcohol, bar snacks
안주.x: What would be good to eat with beer?
안주.e: Literally 'press down the alcohol' — food that softens the drink.
안주.t: Korean bars expect you to order 안주; drinking without food is unusual.

출판.x: That book was published last year.
출판.e: Literally 'putting out from the printing block'.

털털하다.ex: 그녀는 성격이 털털해서 누구와도 잘 어울려요.
털털하다.x: She's easygoing, so she gets along with everyone.

도달하다.m: to reach, to arrive at, to attain
도달하다.ex: 오랜 회의 끝에 드디어 합의에 도달했어요.
도달하다.x: After a long meeting, we finally reached an agreement.

면제되다.m: to be exempted, to be waived
면제되다.x: Scholarship students are exempted from tuition.

몰두하다.m: to be absorbed in, to devote oneself to, to concentrate on
몰두하다.ex: 그는 연구에 몰두해서 밥 먹는 것도 잊었어요.
몰두하다.x: He was so absorbed in his research that he forgot to eat.
몰두하다.t: Pattern: N에 몰두하다, as in 일에 몰두하다 'bury oneself in work'.

빈번하다.x: Traffic accidents happen frequently on this road.
빈번하다.t: A formal word often used in news; in everyday speech people just say 자주.

값지다.x: This failure was a valuable experience for me.
값지다.e: Built from 값 'price, value' + 지다 'to have' — something full of worth.
값지다.t: Pronounced [갑찌다]; usually for experiences or lessons, not prices — use 비싸다 for 'expensive'.

흐름.ex: 시대의 흐름에 따라 생활 방식도 바뀌어요.
흐름.x: Lifestyles change with the flow of the times.
흐름.e: Noun from 흐르다 'to flow': 흐르- plus -ㅁ.
흐름.t: Used for water, time and ideas: 시간의 흐름, 대화의 흐름 'flow of the conversation'.

회신.m: reply, response (formal, e.g. to an email)
회신.t: A formal word for business emails and official letters; with friends use 답장.

소신.x: He stuck to his convictions to the end.
소신.t: Common collocations: 소신을 지키다 'stick to one's convictions' and 소신을 밝히다 'state one's position'.

원전.ex: 정부는 새 원전 건설 계획을 발표했습니다.
원전.x: The government announced a plan to build a new nuclear power plant.
원전.e: Short for 원자력 발전소 'nuclear power station'.
원전.t: 원전 is the standard news abbreviation; in speech people also say 원자력 발전소.

제자.x: The teacher always attends her former students' weddings.
제자.e: Literally 'younger brother and child', a disciple.
제자.t: 제자 implies a personal teacher–student bond; 학생 is the neutral word for student.

비견되다.m: to be compared to, to be on a par with, to rank alongside
비견되다.ex: 그 화가는 피카소에 비견될 만큼 뛰어난 인물입니다.
비견되다.x: That painter is an outstanding figure, comparable to Picasso.
비견되다.t: Usually used with 에: A에 비견되다 = to be mentioned in the same breath as A.

남루하다.ex: 그 노인은 남루한 옷차림으로 길가에 앉아 있었어요.
남루하다.x: The old man was sitting by the road in ragged clothes.
남루하다.e: Literally 'tattered rags' — used mostly for clothing.
남루하다.t: Pronounced [남누하다] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

간사하다.ex: 사람 마음이 참 간사해서 상황이 바뀌면 생각도 바뀌어요.
간사하다.x: People's hearts are so fickle — when the situation changes, so do their thoughts.
간사하다.t: Set phrase 사람 마음이 간사하다 means people change their minds to suit themselves.

포부.x: The new employees announced their aspirations for the new year.
포부.e: Literally 'holding and carrying' — a goal you carry in your heart.
포부.t: Always positive; a staple of interviews: 앞으로의 포부를 말씀해 주세요 'Tell us your aspirations'.

얼떨결에.m: in the confusion, without thinking, on the spur of the moment
얼떨결에.ex: 갑자기 질문을 받아서 얼떨결에 네라고 대답했어요.
얼떨결에.x: I was suddenly asked a question, so I said yes without thinking.
얼떨결에.e: From 얼떨떨하다 'to be dazed' plus 결 'moment, while'.

면모.m: aspect, side (of someone's character); appearance, look
면모.ex: 그는 이번 공연에서 새로운 면모를 보여 줬어요.
면모.x: He showed a new side of himself in this performance.
면모.e: Literally 'face and appearance' — how someone or something presents itself.

동양화.x: East Asian painting is known for its ink and the beauty of empty space.

투지.x: The players never lost their fighting spirit until the very end.

그런가 하면.forms: A. 그런가 하면 B. (a contrasting case or another example)
그런가 하면.m: on the other hand, meanwhile, then again
그런가 하면.ex: 여름을 좋아하는 사람이 있어요. 그런가 하면 겨울만 기다리는 사람도 있죠.
그런가 하면.x: Some people love summer. Then again, there are people who just wait for winter.
그런가 하면.e: 그렇다 'to be so' + -ㄴ가 'is it?' + 하면 'if one thinks': 'just when you think it's so …'.
그런가 하면.t: Somewhat formal; common in essays, news and speeches to bring in a contrasting case or another example.

무국적.ex: 전쟁으로 많은 사람들이 무국적 상태가 되었어요.
무국적.x: Because of the war, many people became stateless.

오차범위.ex: 두 후보의 지지율 차이는 오차범위 안에 있습니다.
오차범위.x: The gap in support between the two candidates is within the margin of error.
오차범위.t: News reports love the phrase 오차범위 내 접전 — a close race within the margin of error.

윤문.ex: 번역 원고를 출판하기 전에 전문가에게 윤문을 맡겼어요.
윤문.x: Before publishing, we had an expert polish the translated manuscript.
윤문.e: Literally 'moistening the writing' — making it read smoothly.
윤문.t: 윤문 polishes a text's style; 교정 fixes typos and other errors.

나전칠기.ex: 할머니 댁에는 오래된 나전칠기 장롱이 있어요.
나전칠기.x: My grandmother's house has an old mother-of-pearl lacquered wardrobe.
나전칠기.e: Shell pieces are inlaid into wood, then coated with lacquer.
나전칠기.t: In everyday speech people often say 자개 for the shell inlay, as in 자개장 (inlaid wardrobe).

폐위.ex: 연산군은 폭정을 일삼다가 결국 신하들에 의해 폐위되었어요.
폐위.x: Yeonsangun ruled as a tyrant and was eventually deposed by his own ministers.

사일구혁명.x: The April 19 Revolution finally forced President Syngman Rhee to step down.
사일구혁명.e: Named after April 19, 1960, when student-led protests toppled the government; usually written 4·19.

상전벽해.m: a complete transformation, drastic change over time
상전벽해.x: This neighborhood has changed beyond recognition in ten years.
상전벽해.e: Literally 'mulberry fields turned into blue sea' — the world changed completely.
상전벽해.t: Pronounced [상전벼캐]; often describes cities or neighborhoods redeveloped beyond recognition.

퇴출되다.m: to be forced out, to be expelled, to be removed
퇴출되다.x: The player who cheated was kicked out of the league.
퇴출되다.t: 퇴출 means being forced out; leaving voluntarily is 탈퇴.

근엄하다.x: The judge read the ruling with a stern expression.

계층이동.x: Education is called the ladder of social mobility.
계층이동.t: Common phrase: 계층이동 사다리가 끊어졌다, 'the ladder of social mobility is broken'.

치하하다.m: to commend, to praise (a subordinate's work)
치하하다.x: The president commended the rescue workers for their hard work.
치하하다.e: Literally 'convey congratulations' — a superior praising effort.
치하하다.t: Used by a superior toward subordinates; you wouldn't 치하 your boss. 노고를 치하하다 is a set phrase.

사무치다.m: to pierce deeply (into the heart), to be deeply felt
사무치다.ex: 고향에 계신 어머니가 뼈에 사무치게 그리워요.
사무치다.x: I miss my mother back home so much it aches in my bones.
사무치다.e: From an old verb meaning 'to get through' — a feeling that goes all the way through.
사무치다.t: Fixed patterns: 뼈에 사무치다, 한이 사무치다, 사무치게 그립다 — for feelings that cut to the core.

요염하다.ex: 그 배우는 영화에서 요염한 눈빛 연기로 화제가 됐어요.
요염하다.x: The actress became the talk of the town for her seductive gaze in the film.

층층이.m: in layers, tier upon tier; on every floor
층층이.x: The boxes are stacked in layers in the warehouse.

도래.m: advent, arrival (of an era or age)
도래.ex: 인공지능 시대의 도래로 일자리가 변하고 있어요.
도래.x: With the advent of the AI era, jobs are changing.
도래.t: Used for eras and ages (새 시대가 도래하다), not for people arriving.

뇌척수액.x: The doctor collected cerebrospinal fluid for testing.
